The '''Union Language Committee''' is the Zhensanov language-policy body source-attested as responsible for developing the [[Union Alphabet]].

== Role ==

The committee's main 1994-back significance is script standardization. In the source set, it developed the Union Alphabet to provide a common writing system for the [[Zhensanovian Languages]], especially for official documents, education, signage, and media. The exact pre-1994 implementation scope remains open.

This draft does not define the committee's legal status, membership, or exact relationship to the [[Zhensanov United Party]] because the current source does not provide those details.

== Later Trajectory ==

Later source material connects the committee to Sanovic, a constructed lingua franca described as early twenty-first-century. That later language work is outside the 1994-back pass and should be reviewed separately.
